svg.title: Spherical aberration
svg.desc: Parallel rays at different heights pass through a converging lens with spherical surfaces. Rays through the outer zones of the lens are bent more and cross the axis closer to the lens than rays near the axis, so there is no single focal point. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: Same spherical lens; iris blocks outer rays
Exact spherical-surface traces, with the screen near the paraxial focus. This isolates geometric
blur; very small apertures also cause diffraction (chapter 27).
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
